name: user-delegation-runtime
status: integration guidance; enable only after independent domain authorities and receiver transaction enforcement are ready
guide:
# User delegation deployment and integration

This is a User-side implementation. Knowledge and Agent must implement the independent
authority endpoint described in `contracts/user/auth-delegation-v1.json`; a proof
reference is only a lookup key. Their durable facts must establish the actual user,
session, resource access, parent/root lineage, run epoch and current worker. A safe
checkpoint additionally needs an already-started step and operation identity. Manual
continue requires an explicit action under a new active session and an authority-side
atomic epoch advance. The User service cannot enforce those domain facts for them.

## Configuration

- Configure the existing User signing keys and service policy first. Add a
  `knode-user` service credential hash with `auth:proofs:read` for both
  `knode-knowledge` and `knode-agent`; grant each caller only its required
  `auth:delegations:issue`, `auth:delegations:validate`, or
  `auth:delegations:validate-checkpoint` machine permissions. Distribute matching
  public verification keys through your approved key distribution.
- Set exactly one of `KNODE_DELEGATION_POLICY_FILE` and
  `KNODE_DELEGATION_POLICY_ENV`. The latter names an environment variable
  containing the JSON. Start from `contracts/user/delegation-policy.example.json`
  and restrict operations to the deployed agreement. With no policy, delegation is disabled.
- Set `KNODE_DELEGATION_KNOWLEDGE_ORIGIN` and
  `KNODE_DELEGATION_AGENT_ORIGIN` to server-controlled origins. HTTPS is required,
  except literal loopback HTTP for isolated testing. Origins cannot contain credentials,
  paths, queries or fragments. The fixed proof path is appended by User; redirects
  are rejected. Missing origins fail closed.
- Supply exactly one of `KNODE_DELEGATION_OUTBOUND_SECRET_FILE` and
  `KNODE_DELEGATION_OUTBOUND_SECRET_ENV`; the latter names an environment variable
  containing the credential. Use an externally provisioned secret matching the User
  service policy, not the example values. Never put credentials or tokens in contracts,
  URLs, logs or version control.
- Provision `db/V007__delegation_grants.sql` only against a separately authorized
  new User database, after reviewing the target and backup procedure. It is not
  automatically executed. The tables contain session and resource identifiers;
  apply your normal access and retention controls.

Each proof request is a fixed POST with a User machine bearer for the receiving
authority and `auth:proofs:read`. User permits four simultaneous outbound proof
requests, with a two-second bound and a 16 KiB response cap. Timeout, redirect,
malformed response, unavailable session or database produce a fail-closed error;
an explicit authority denial produces 403. Proofs cannot widen a persisted root
envelope. The receiver should continue checking its own live resource authority.

## Receiver integration

Use the CPU-only `knode-auth` verifier. `verifyNormal` and `verifyCheckpoint`
produce distinct verified types and do not themselves authorize. Independently
verify the actor machine token, fetch current authority and persisted grant facts,
then call the matching authorization method. Ordinary authorization also requires
the current ACTIVE session. The online User validation endpoints perform those
checks centrally when that is the agreed integration boundary.

The separate checkpoint type is not general authorization. Its receiver must lock
or compare-and-set the live run, epoch and worker, deduplicate both jti and checkpoint
operation ID, bind the result digest, and commit the checkpoint effect in the same
local transaction. Identical retries may return already applied; changed digest,
worker or epoch must fail. User's checkpoint validation is not evidence that the
receiver transaction committed. See `LocalCheckpointReceiverFixture` for an
isolated example, not a production Agent implementation.

## Local verification

Run the reactor from the repository root so the current shared SDK is built:

```text
mvn -pl knode-user -am test -B -ntp
```

The HTTP integration fixture uses synthetic identities, its own local H2 authority
facts and a loopback random port. Its optional MySQL test properties must point only
to a separately created isolated test instance; never point them at a shared database
or real data.

## Checkpoint authority and issuance retry

Agent must prove from persisted current facts that the step actually started, its
run, epoch, worker, step and operation match, and the step save window and worker
lease remain active. The Agent proof validUntil must not exceed either real window;
a guessed future timestamp or caller-supplied identity is not evidence. Reject
not-started, expired, revoked or superseded facts.

Issuance requires an unexpired normal parent and active subject. Its separately
signed checkpoint may outlive the parent transport token, bounded by 300 seconds
and every applicable authorization, original session, machine and safety deadline.
One operation cannot be issued twice: a lost issuance response is not recoverable
by retrying issuance. An already-held capability may be retried only through the
receiver's atomic operation/jti/digest and current epoch/worker transaction.
